title: AI Meets Maritime Training: Precision Analytics for Enhanced Safety and Performance
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a problem in simulator-based maritime training: instructor assessments of trainees’ technical skills, communication, attention, and stress are often subjective and difficult to standardize. The authors argue that traditional training lacks objective ways to measure key human factors such as visual focus, checklist adherence in communication, and stress response during high-risk scenarios, which are important for safety-critical maritime work.

To address this, the study develops an AI-driven assessment framework that combines multiple analytic components: computer vision and eye tracking to identify which panels and subpanels trainees attend to, an attentional focus metric based on pupil dilation and gaze stability, a maritime-adapted speech recognition system for domain-specific communication, named entity recognition for identifying communication targets, a large language model to judge checklist adherence in emergency communications, and an audio-based stress detection model. The framework is demonstrated on data collected in a maritime navigation simulator, including scenarios with good visibility and reduced visibility and events such as engine failure, potential collisions, and squalls.

The population consists of maritime simulator participants described as seafarers/trainees in Singapore, using the Advanced Navigation Research Simulator at the Centre of Excellence in Maritime Safety, Singapore. The paper reports strong technical performance for the component models, including about 95.04% panel detection accuracy, 98% validation accuracy for the communication classification approach cited from related work by the authors, and 90.33% stress detection accuracy. The evaluation section also includes a case-study-style analysis of one subject across two simulated conditions, illustrating how the dashboard can identify changes in attention, communication behavior, checklist adherence, and stress over time.

The main conclusion is that AI-based multimodal analytics can make maritime simulator training more objective and actionable by providing trainers with detailed performance information and identifying areas for personalized feedback. However, the paper does not present a controlled comparison of learning outcomes against another training approach, and its empirical demonstration is primarily a technical validation and case-study-style framework evaluation rather than a comparative effectiveness study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is conference grey literature outside K-12 education, with no controlled comparative design, no clear participant sample reporting, and no direct educational impact estimates. It primarily reports algorithm accuracy and an illustrative case study rather than credible causal evidence about learning or feedback effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially useful but unclear impact through improved assessment analytics in maritime simulator training, yet it provides no effect sizes or controlled evidence of improvement in learner outcomes. For the target question on ChatGPT writing feedback in grades 9-12, impact is effectively non-informative and only very distantly adjacent.

interventions.use_case: AI-driven multimodal performance analytics for maritime simulator training, combining eye tracking/computer vision, speech recognition, LLM-based checklist adherence analysis, and vocal stress detection to generate objective trainer feedback.
Simulator-based maritime navigation exercises used as the training environment in which AI analytics assess trainee behavior under controlled high-stress scenarios.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports strong technical performance for AI-based assessment components in a maritime vocational training context rather than student learning gains. Panel detection achieved 95.04% validation performance, maritime speech recognition/checklist-related classification reached 98% validation accuracy, and stress detection reached 90.33% accuracy, outperforming comparison models reported at 76%, 76%, and 89%.
finding.measure: Model validation accuracy for panel detection, maritime speech recognition / communication correctness classification, and stress detection

finding.finding_summary: The system appears to improve objectivity and granularity of simulator assessment by automatically surfacing visual attention, checklist adherence, communication targets, and stress patterns for trainers. However, the evidence is based on system performance metrics and illustrative case-study dashboard outputs rather than controlled estimates of time savings, reliability gains, or workload reduction for instructors.
finding.measure: Assessment automation/objective analytics dashboard outputs; detection and classification accuracy

finding.finding_summary: The case-study dashboard suggests the framework can identify aspects of trainee situational awareness, communication completeness, and response under stress in simulated emergency conditions. But the paper does not provide pre-post or comparative evidence that the AI system improves these underlying human performance skills; it only shows that the system can measure them and highlight omissions such as failure to notify nearby ships or prepare anchoring stations.
finding.measure: Observed checklist adherence, communication behavior, visual focus, and inferred attentional focus during simulator tasks
